title: Key Personnel: what constrains filling and keeping an opening at a small technical firm whose hires must satisfy a contract or a customer, what the evidence says each lever does, and which gates bind
question: For a small technical firm whose hires must satisfy a contract or a customer, what actually constrains filling and keeping a position at each stage from workforce planning to handover; what does the evidence say each lever does and does not do; which regulatory and contractual gates bind a given opening; how do the constraints depend on one another; and what public data, programs and tools can a recruiter without an HR department put to work?
venue: Commissioned guide — NOT PEER REVIEWED, NOT LEGAL, HR OR COMPLIANCE ADVICE. Written by an AI research builder from published studies and public government sources for a public audience; every record links to the study or the governing text it rests on. No connection with any firm.
plain_abstract: Key Personnel is a map for whoever has to fill and keep a position at a small technical firm when a contract, a labor category, a clearance or a customer's approval decides who may hold it. It starts from what the recruiter is seeing, many applicants but few who qualify, candidates who withdraw, offers declined, hires who cannot start, people who struggle or leave, a customer who rejects, and narrows sixty evidence-graded constraints to the ones that fit the opening, then draws how they depend on one another as a graph whose every edge is cited. Each constraint carries the levers the firm can pull, with the effect sizes as the studies reported them and what each lever has not been shown to do; the regulatory and contractual gates that bind, from the Uniform Guidelines to clearance sponsorship to the state pay-posting and noncompete laws; the public data behind the benchmarks; and a dated record of what changed in 2025 and 2026. The author's own sixty guesses about staffing were tested against the evidence and the ledger is published. Written by an AI research builder from 312 sources read as of 22 October 2026; not peer reviewed; not advice.
audience: a recruiter, hiring lead or owner at a small technical firm with no HR department, whose hires must satisfy a labor category, a key-personnel clause, a rate ceiling, a clearance or a customer approval; a second layer for the experienced contracts or security manager
